brief:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu achieved a long-standing goal by securing direct military strikes against Iran, but the outcome may have weakened Israel's regional position rather than strengthened it, according to Al-Monitor. After six months of hostilities between Israel and Iranian targets, the campaign has produced inconclusive results that fall short of the strategic objectives Netanyahu pursued throughout decades of urging American military intervention.

The operation has left Israeli security planners reassessing whether the strikes advanced their interests or instead complicated an already volatile situation in the Middle East. Military analysts now question whether the campaign's limited success justifies the risks Israel accepted by directly engaging Iranian forces and infrastructure.

title: Netanyahu's Iran campaign fails to deliver strategic gains
